Obranome in this sense is an authentic visual metabolism of the word and of the object understood as a living organism. The genealogical trace of obranome undoubtedly goes back to the ready mades of Marcel Duchamp, to Mallarmé’s spatial poem, Marcel, or to the intermediary poetry of Dick Higgins, belonging to the Fluxus movement. Yet without leaving the ambit of his own country, Wagner Barja inserts himself in a specific Brazilian tradition that runs from concretism and neoconcretism to visual poetry. In the first place, “Cubo Cruz Lápide” (1985), as has already been shown, literally fulfills the announced organic character of the bichos that Lygia Clark had made in the sixties, geometric structures of anodized aluminum that can, thanks precisely to the hinges, adopt multiple, living and asymmetrical forms. A metamorphosis of geometric reason into biology through the piece that, with its own movement, pierces space and allows the direct participation of the public: “total, existential integration, established between it, the Bicho, and us, the manipulators of the hand-to-hand between two living entities” (20). In my opinion, the concept of obranome proposed by Barja partakes of all the characteristics that Ferreira Gullar points out for its definition in the object: immanence, the signified derived from the form itself, unity, without, through it, significantly renouncing the name. The concept of obranome is, literally, transparent because it definitively incorporates the name into the thing. From something exterior, clarifying the object that it is – which is, in general, the function and the necessity of naming – Barja performs an operation that definitively includes it in the very process of the work, of the object. “Cubo Cruz Lápide” (1985) becomes a visual crystallization of the image and of the word that devours the information contained; in the interior of the cube-cross-book, the words and the image feed each other. A dialectic at the borderline where the object and language, by proximity, feed each other and release bundles of unexpected luminosity one upon the other, until generating another aesthetic object.
